Great Keep.summary: The [Great Keep](Great_Keep_%28Winterfell%29) is the innermost castle and stronghold of the castle complex. It was built over natural hot springs to keep it warm. The Great Keep contains bedchambers for [House Stark](House_Stark) as well as the [solar](Solar) of Lord [Eddard Stark](Eddard_Stark). The building is connected to the armory by a covered bridge. From a window on the bridge, one can see the entire yard. Beneath the Great Keep are cellars with narrow windows.

Great Hall.summary: The [Great Hall](Great_Hall_of_Winterfell) is used for receiving guests and the place where the household dines together, including the [Lord of Winterfell](Lord_of_Winterfell). It is made of grey stone and has wide doors made of [oak](Oak) and [iron](Iron), which opens to the castle yard, and a rear exit leads to a dimly-lit gallery. Inside, it can hold eight long rows of trestle tables, four to each side of the central aisle, and the hall can seat five hundred people. There is a raised platform for noble guests, and the walls are covered with banners. The hall contains the high seat of the old [Kings in the North](King_in_the_North). The seat's cold stone has been polished by the many lords who have sat upon it, and its massive arms are decorated with the carved heads of snarling [direwolves](Direwolf).

First Keep.summary: The [First Keep](First_Keep), a squat and round drum tower, is the oldest surviving part of the castle but is no longer in use. Around it lies a [lichyard](Lichyard) where the [Kings of Winter](King_in_the_North) would bury their loyal servants. The keep has [gargoyles](Gargoyle) atop it. Maester [Kennet](Kennet_%28maester%29) determined it was built after the [Andals](Andals) arrived.

Broken Tower.summary: The [broken tower](Broken_tower), also known as the Burned Tower, was once the tallest watchtower in Winterfell. Over 140 years ago a lightning strike set it afire and the top third collapsed inward, but no one rebuilt it. It stands behind the old inner ward. [Crows](Crow) nest atop the broken tower.

Library Tower.summary: The [Library Tower](Library_Tower) houses the library at Winterfell. A stonework staircase winds about its exterior.

Bell Tower.summary: The [Bell Tower](Bell_Tower) is connected to the [rookery](Rookery) by a bridge. The bridge is covered and runs from the fourth floor of the tower to the second floor of the rookery.

Maester's Turret.summary: [Maester Luwin's turret](Maester_Luwin's_turret) is below the rookery.

Guards Hall.summary: The [Guards Hall](Guards_Hall) is in line with the Bell Tower, and further back, the First Keep.

Glass Gardens.summary: The [Glass Gardens](Glass_Gardens) is a greenhouse heated by the hot springs, which turn it into a place of moist warmth. It is used to grow fruits, vegetables, and flowers. The garden has green and yellow glass panes locked in frames.

Godswood.summary: The ancient [godswood of Winterfell](Godswood_of_Winterfell) has stood untouched for ten thousand years, with three acres of old packed earth and close-together trees creating a dense canopy, which the castle was built around. At the center of the grove stands an ancient [weirwood](Weirwood) with [a face carved into it](Heart_tree), standing over a pool of black water. Across the godswood from the heart tree, beneath the windows of the [Guest House](Guest_House), an underground hot spring feeds three small pools, with a moss-covered wall looming above them. The godswood is enclosed by walls, and is accessed by a main iron gate, or smaller wooden ones.

Heart Tree.summary: At the center of the grove stands an ancient [weirwood](Weirwood) with [a face carved into it](Heart_tree), standing over a pool of black water.

Crypts.summary: The [crypt of Winterfell](Crypts_of_Winterfell), located near the First Keep, is where members of [House Stark](House_Stark) are buried. The underground crypts are long and narrow, with pillars moving two by two along its length. Between pillars stand the sepulchers of the Starks of Winterfell, the likenesses of the dead seated on thrones, with [iron swords](Iron_swords) set before them to keep the [restless spirits](Ghosts) from wandering, and snarling [direwolves](Direwolf) at their feet. The crypts are deep under the earth, cavernous and bigger than the complex above ground. They are accessed by a twisting stone stair and a huge ironwood door that lies at a slant to the floor. The stair continues below to older levels where the most ancient [Kings in the North](King_in_the_North) are entombed.

South Gate.summary: The great [main gates of Winterfell](Main_gates_of_Winterfell) have a gatehouse made of two huge crenelated bulwarks which flank the arched gate and a drawbridge that opens into the market square of the [winter town](Winter_town).

Hunter's Gate.summary: The [Hunter's Gate](Hunter's_Gate) is close to the kennels and the [kitchens of Winterfell](Kitchens_of_Winterfell). It opens directly onto open fields and the [wolfswood](Wolfswood), so people can come and go without having to cross through the winter town. It is favored by hunting parties.

East Gate.summary: The [East Gate](East_Gate) or east gate leads to the [kingsroad](Kingsroad). The Kingsroad Gate may be another name for the same gate.

Moat.summary: Winterfell is a huge castle complex spanning several acres, defended by two massive walls of grey granite with a wide moat between them.

Winter Town.summary: The [winter town](Winter_town), so called because it is mostly deserted during summer, is where smallfolk gather in winter. It is outside the walls of Winterfell. Its market square is filled with wooden stalls for merchants, and its streets are muddy and lined with rows of houses made from logs and undressed stone. Less than one in five are occupied during the summer, but they fill up when winter arrives. The kingsroad, which runs east of Winterfell, is beyond the winter town. There is an inn in the winter town, the [Smoking Log](Smoking_Log).

The Red Keep.summary: The [Red Keep](Red_Keep), the royal castle located on top of Aegon's High Hill. Within the castle are [Maegor's Holdfast](Maegor's_Holdfast) and the [Tower of the Hand](Tower_of_the_Hand).

Great Sept of Baelor.summary: The [Great Sept of Baelor](Great_Sept_of_Baelor), where the [Most Devout](Most_Devout) convene with the [High Septon](High_Septon). It is the holiest sept of the [Faith of the Seven](Faith_of_the_Seven). It is located on Visenya's Hill.

Dragonpit.summary: The [Dragonpit](Dragonpit), a huge dome, now collapsed, that used to hold the Targaryen dragons. Its bronze doors have not been opened for more than a century. It is found on the Hill of Rhaenys. The Street of Sisters runs between it and the Great Sept of Baelor.

Guildhall of the Alchemists.summary: The [Guildhall of the Alchemists](Guildhall_of_the_Alchemists) beneath the Hill of Rhaenys, stretching right to the foot of Visenya's Hill, along the Street of Sisters. Beneath it is where the Alchemists create and store the [wildfire](Wildfire).

Flea Bottom.summary: [Flea Bottom](Flea_Bottom), slum area of King's Landing, a downtrodden area of town. It has pot-shops along the alleys where one can get a [bowl of brown](Bowl_of_brown). It has a stench of pigsties and stables, tanner's sheds mixed in the smell of winesinks and whorehouses.

Shae's Manse.summary: A [manse near the Iron Gate](Manse_near_the_Iron_Gate) with its own stable, well, and garden.

Littlefinger's Brothel.summary: Lord [Petyr Baelish](Petyr_Baelish) owns [a brothel](Petyr_Baelish's_brothel) near the river.

Fishmonger's Square.summary: [Fishmonger's Square](Fishmonger's_Square) is a market square inside the Mud Gate.

Tourney Grounds.summary: The [tourney grounds](Tourney_grounds_%28King's_Landing%29) outside the city are near the Blackwater and the [King's Gate](King's_Gate).

Aegon's High Hill.summary: [Aegon's High Hill](Aegon's_High_Hill), surmounted by the [Red Keep](Red_Keep), the royal castle located in the south-eastern corner of the city, overlooks the bay directly, whilst [Visenya's Hill](Visenya's_Hill) to the west is crowned by the [marble](Marble)-walled [Great Sept of Baelor](Great_Sept_of_Baelor) and its seven crystal towers.

Visenya's Hill.summary: [Aegon's High Hill](Aegon's_High_Hill), surmounted by the [Red Keep](Red_Keep), the royal castle located in the south-eastern corner of the city, overlooks the bay directly, whilst [Visenya's Hill](Visenya's_Hill) to the west is crowned by the [marble](Marble)-walled [Great Sept of Baelor](Great_Sept_of_Baelor) and its seven crystal towers.

Rhaenys's Hill.summary: The [Hill of Rhaenys](Hill_of_Rhaenys) in the north is capped by the collapsed ruins of the [Dragonpit](Dragonpit) dome, its bronze doors shut for a century and a half since the last dragon died.

Street of Steel.summary: The [Street of Steel](Street_of_Steel) is where most smiths have their forges. It begins on the west of Fishmonger's Square inside the River Gate and climbs up Visenya's Hill. The higher up one goes, the more expensive the shops. At its top is the [shop of Tobho Mott](Shop_of_Tobho_Mott).

Street of Silk.summary: The [Street of Silk](Street_of_Silk) is a street to the northwest of the Dragonpit lined with brothels of varying expense, including [Chataya's](Chataya's_brothel).

Street of the Sisters.summary: The [Street of the Sisters](Street_of_the_Sisters) connects the [Great Sept of Baelor](Great_Sept_of_Baelor) to the [Dragonpit](Dragonpit). One can find the [Guildhall of the Alchemists](Guildhall_of_the_Alchemists) upon it. It runs straight as an arrow between the hills of Rhaenys and Visenya, from which it gets its name.

Muddy Way.summary: The [Muddy Way](Muddy_Way), formerly known as "Blackwater Way". It begins at Fishmonger's Square.

The Hook.summary: The [Hook](Hook) is a long, curved thoroughfare connecting the River Gate to Aegon's High Hill.

River Row.summary: [River Row](River_Row) is a street along the southern wall, east of Fishmonger's Square, home to sea captains, fishmongers and others with interest in the harbor.

River Gate.summary: [River Gate](River_Gate), known as the Mud Gate by the population of the city, leads south to the [kingsroad](Kingsroad) and the [roseroad](Roseroad).
